provenance: AI-assisted synthetic research cases authored for this experiment before API outcome inspection. Not interviews, logs, representative population samples, or independently validated gold standards.
scope: Administrative coordination and shared caregiving; not replacement of care or medical decisions.
design: Eight activities, two decisions, four exceptions, four actors, four systems, four inputs, four outputs and three candidate support opportunities per case. Artificial regularity is a limitation.

scenarios.title: Morning Preparation and Childcare Drop-off
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I get my child ready in the morning, pack what we need, and take them to childcare. If we are running late, I let someone know.

reference_workflow.goal: Morning Preparation and Childcare Drop-off with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Check the arrival window and provider notice
Confirm the escort with the partner
Review the daily item list
Pack and check the bag
Resolve missing items before departure
Escort the child to childcare
Send an arrival delay notice when needed
Confirm handover with the childcare teacher

branches: check the agreed substitute or contact the teacher

decisions.condition: Can the assigned escort meet the arrival window?
branches: confirm the backup caregiver and notify the teacher

automation_opportunities.rationale: Combine calendar reminders and provider notices for parent review.
Generate a dated packing checklist without confirming physical completion.
Draft delay messages for the parent's confirmation.

operating_context.manual_effort: Checklist review and calendar coordination take about ten minutes in this fictional household.
operating_context.data_availability: The calendar is shared with the partner; childcare messages remain in the provider app.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: A reminder may be drafted automatically, but a parent confirms any escort change; handover remains in person.

reference_workflow.interpretation: Activity dependencies describe the nominal sequence. Decision branches and exception descriptions qualify that sequence; this is not an executable BPMN model.

unknown_information: Numeric arrival times, monetary amounts and product specifications not explicitly provided are unknown.
No medical judgments, real child records or legal policy claims are represented.

scenarios.title: Afternoon Pickup and Caregiver Handover
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I arrange who will pick up my child and check that they got home. Sometimes the person collecting them changes during the day.

reference_workflow.goal: Afternoon Pickup and Caregiver Handover with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Review the pickup window
Ask the planned collector to confirm availability
Check the collector against authorized pickup names
Request a collector change from the teacher if needed
Wait for provider acknowledgment before the changed pickup
Collect the child and confirm collection
Record home arrival in the handover log
Follow up on a missing collection confirmation

decisions.condition: Is the proposed collector already authorized?
Has collection been confirmed by the end of the pickup window?
branches: contact the collector and the teacher

automation_opportunities.rationale: Summarize pickup plans from the household calendar.
Send availability requests to the planned collector.
Remind the mother when a confirmation has not been logged.

operating_context.manual_effort: The mother spends about five minutes confirming pickup when the original plan holds.
operating_context.data_availability: The household can read its calendar and handover log, but only the provider updates the pickup list.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: A new collector is not automatically approved; the teacher follows the fictional provider's agreed acknowledgment process.

reference_workflow.interpretation: Activity dependencies describe the nominal sequence. Decision branches and exception descriptions qualify that sequence; this is not an executable BPMN model.

scenarios.title: Childcare Notices and Consent Responses
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I read messages from childcare, respond when necessary, and make sure we remember any special event or item to bring.

reference_workflow.goal: Childcare Notices and Consent Responses with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Collect unread notices from the provider app
Identify response and preparation requirements
Check the event against the household schedule
Ask the administrator about unclear notice details
Confirm the family's participation decision
Submit a response and save the receipt
Add the event and item deadline to the calendar
Check that the preparation reminder is assigned

decisions.condition: Does the notice require an explicit response?
branches: record the notice without a response

decisions.condition: Are the event details complete and compatible with the schedule?
branches: clarify missing details or decline participation

automation_opportunities.rationale: Extract proposed dates and preparation requirements for review.
Draft calendar entries from confirmed notices.
Flag unassigned preparation reminders.

operating_context.frequency: notices checked once each evening in this fictional household
operating_context.manual_effort: Reading and recording a routine notice takes about five minutes.
operating_context.data_availability: Notices and response receipts are accessible in the provider app; the family manually copies dates into its calendar.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: Consent is always confirmed by a parent; summaries cannot submit consent or disclose notices to unrelated recipients.

reference_workflow.interpretation: Activity dependencies describe the nominal sequence. Decision branches and exception descriptions qualify that sequence; this is not an executable BPMN model.

scenarios.title: Family Outing Preparation and Return
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: Before going out with my child, I get our things together and coordinate with whoever is coming. Afterwards I put things away for next time.

reference_workflow.goal: Family Outing Preparation and Return with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Check the outing time and venue information
Confirm who will accompany the child
Prepare the outing checklist
Check reusable items against the inventory
Pack and confirm needed items
Resolve missing items or change the outing plan
Notify accompanying caregivers of plan changes
Record used items and restock the bag after returning

decisions.condition: Are the venue plan and accompanying caregiver confirmed?
branches: contact the venue or rearrange the plan
obtain an agreed substitute or postpone

automation_opportunities.rationale: Create an outing checklist from the confirmed plan.
Draft one consistent plan-change message.
Create restocking reminders from recorded usage.

operating_context.frequency: one planned outing most weekends in this fictional household
operating_context.manual_effort: Checking and packing usually takes about fifteen minutes, excluding travel.
operating_context.data_availability: The family keeps an item list but it does not detect physical stock automatically.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: Checklists can be suggested; physical item checks and the decision to change the outing remain with caregivers.

scenarios.title: Weekly Shared Caregiving Schedule
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I work out next week's childcare arrangements with my family. When someone cannot make it, we find another arrangement and tell each other.

reference_workflow.goal: Weekly Shared Caregiving Schedule with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Collect adult availability for the coming week
List care periods outside childcare hours
Match each care period with an available adult
Request explicit acceptance from assigned caregivers
Find a replacement for an uncovered period
Publish the agreed schedule in the shared calendar
Notify affected caregivers of any later change
Record acknowledgment of the revised assignment

decisions.condition: Is every required care period assigned to an available adult?
Has the assigned caregiver accepted the period?
branches: keep it pending and contact the caregiver

automation_opportunities.rationale: Identify time periods requiring care from agreed schedules.
Suggest nonconflicting assignments for family review.
Track missing acknowledgment after a schedule change.

operating_context.frequency: schedule prepared every Sunday and updated when availability changes
operating_context.manual_effort: Initial coordination takes about twenty minutes in this fictional household.
operating_context.data_availability: Adults provide their availability voluntarily; the shared table records accepted versus pending assignments.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: Software may suggest an assignment but cannot treat silence as acceptance or override a caregiver's availability.

scenarios.title: Childcare Supply Stock and Replenishment
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I check the supplies we use for my child and order more when they are getting low. When the delivery arrives, I put everything away.

reference_workflow.goal: Childcare Supply Stock and Replenishment with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Count the available household supplies
Compare counts with household reorder thresholds
Check proposed items against the approved product list
Review the basket against the spending limit
Resolve unavailable products with a parent
Place the confirmed order and save confirmation
Check the delivery against the order record
Store items and update the inventory count

decisions.condition: Is the stock below the household reorder threshold?
branches: leave the item off the order

decisions.condition: Does the basket meet product and spending constraints?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Flag items below the household's recorded threshold.
Calculate proposed basket cost and flag the limit.
Draft inventory updates from confirmed delivery quantities.

operating_context.frequency: stock checked twice a week in this fictional household
operating_context.manual_effort: Counting and preparing a shopping list takes about ten minutes.
operating_context.data_availability: Thresholds and product choices are household-defined entries; online stock is visible but not synchronized to the inventory.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: Purchase and product substitution need parent confirmation; no child health or dietary suitability is inferred.

scenarios.title: Evening Caregiver Handover and Next-day Preparation
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: When another family member takes over in the evening, I tell them what still needs doing. We also get things ready for the next day.

reference_workflow.goal: Evening Caregiver Handover and Next-day Preparation with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: List the unfinished household care tasks
Review the next-day schedule
Share relevant caregiver notes with the incoming caregiver
Confirm who accepts each remaining task
Clarify conflicting or missing task information
Prepare items needed for the next day
Mark completed preparation tasks in the checklist
Confirm unresolved tasks with the next-day caregiver

decisions.condition: Has the incoming caregiver acknowledged the remaining tasks?
branches: confirm directly before leaving tasks assigned

decisions.condition: Are next-day items and task owners confirmed?
branches: leave unresolved items open and contact the owner

automation_opportunities.rationale: Draft the open-task list from checked records.
Generate a next-day preparation checklist.
Remind assigned caregivers about unresolved tasks.

operating_context.frequency: each evening when care responsibility changes in this fictional household
operating_context.manual_effort: Updating notes and confirming tasks takes about ten minutes.
operating_context.data_availability: Only participating caregivers can read the shared log; task completion is manually recorded.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: A tool can summarize notes but cannot mark care performed or substitute for an acknowledged human handover.

scenarios.title: Child Activity Enrollment and Schedule Changes
scenarios.narrator: mother in a fictional household with shared caregiving
scenarios.initial_description: I find an activity for my child, sign up if it fits, and put it on our calendar. If the provider changes the schedule, I rearrange our plans.

reference_workflow.goal: Child Activity Enrollment and Schedule Changes with explicit responsibilities, decisions and recorded completion.

activities.name: Collect the activity schedule and participation requirements
Check household and transport caregiver availability
Compare the activity cost with the spending limit
Confirm the participation decision with the partner
Submit the approved registration request
Save provider confirmation before marking enrollment complete
Assign transport and add the activity to the calendar
Confirm revised arrangements after a provider schedule change

decisions.condition: Do schedule and cost fit the household's agreed constraints?
Has the provider confirmed enrollment or the revised schedule?
branches: update the calendar and notify caregivers
keep the arrangement pending and contact the provider

automation_opportunities.rationale: Flag calendar conflicts and missing transport availability.
Track unconfirmed registration requests.
Draft calendar changes and caregiver notifications.

operating_context.frequency: enrollment considered at the start of a term, with occasional provider changes
operating_context.manual_effort: Checking schedules and completing a request takes about fifteen minutes in this fictional household.
operating_context.data_availability: Requirements and availability are shown on the provider page; confirmation is saved separately by the family.
operating_context.integration_and_approval_constraints: Registration and payments need parent approval; a suggested calendar entry is not evidence of provider confirmation.
